# Semantic roles and scope — 2026-11-13

**Q02/Q04/Q07/Q08 pass the targeted execution and condition/disposition checks in shared attempt 2/5.** Stop here; three authorized attempts remain unused. This continuation consumed one new four-case run. No retries, separate semantic judge, commit or push.

## What changed

- Parser and auditor now receive the same complete Typesense semantic catalog snapshot, loaded once per request. Snapshot hash/entries are carried in graph state; audit never reloads a newer revision or retries a failed load. Catalog failure keeps required recommendation validation unavailable; reference-only requests may continue.
- Canonical schema distinguishes the material of a new candidate from existing household context and an independently requested hard compatibility target. Parser compatibility criteria now use `target_type`, separately from pair-reference fields; current callers/tests changed together. No old-field fallback was added. Explicit hard/hypothetical compatibility stays binding; optional or negated candidate material does not become a positive exact filter.
- Environmental suitability is representable without claiming an intrinsic personality trait. Pair-scoped positive agreements remain on their stated pair; non-applicability to another pair does not become an explicit false agreement.
- The authored searchable catalog now has 26 definitions/contrasts, including optional pair scope. Generic examples use other materials; benchmark questions/expectations and all eleven stone fixtures are unchanged. The catalog intentionally changed: **14/15 fixture hashes unchanged**, one catalog revision updated. No persistent local catalog/database reset was performed.

Luna implemented the semantic change. The parent completed remaining test typing/count assertions after a usage interruption; Sol 6.1 High resumed and approved the final diff and live records. Local full suite: **229 passed, 5 opt-in skipped**; Ruff and mypy **105 files** passed. Final catalog/semantic targeted checks: seven passed. Sol independently passed **193 checks** (all 192 unit tests plus disposable Typesense roundtrip) and verified shared revision/no retry behavior.
